_about: Claude I's region plan for Neon Harbour, the delta, the Lull belt, Lullford and Gullwick, as data (docs/vision/regions/neon-harbour-delta.md, world plan v5.3). World px on the 11264 x 6912 continent. 'brief' items are copied from the brief; 'derived' geometry is Claude I's reading of the brief's own coordinates until Claude A's v5.3 block-out (P1) is published as data, then it moves to fit that. Painters: scripts/art/regions/lull_delta.py (the belt, Lullford and the delta). Move a thing to fit the ground, not the ground to fit the number.

source.blockout: not yet published as data; geometry below is derived

lull-delta.why: the belt, Lullford and the delta painted as one chunk: the Lull runs through all three, so one canvas keeps the river, its banks and the bridge seamless. Covers the Lullford box, the belt and delta box, and the land between them west of the delta down to the coast.

tiers.note: brief 4: the belt and delta walk tiers 2 to 5, flat, crossed on boardwalks and the canal embankment; Lullford on a gravel terrace one tier up. v1 paints the floodplain on tier 2 and keeps every height change inside the water pieces (cut banks, canal coping); the terrace under Lullford waits for the cliff core (#165) for its face.

lull.why: six unequal bends (radii 115 to 285, width 110 to 130, plan 4.3) from the braided reach to Lullford Bridge at (8960, 4310), then the delta apex

fresh_oxbow.why: hard by the outer bend at (9330, 3560); the bell in the oxbow is reserved at (9450, 3900) on its far side

silted_oxbow.why: older, further out on the west side, silted to reeds

delta_arms.why: plan 4.3: eight reaches from one apex below Lullford, the widest about 70 px; reed beds between, mudflats in front, a sandbar at each mouth, a lobed front

lull_cut.towpath: north-east (the Delta Road, lane G line)
lull_cut.why: plan 4.3: from Lullford's east bank to the canal basin under the Heights, clear of the delta's silt; it runs 48 px south-west of the Delta Road, which is its towpath

sea.why: the delta builds a lobed front into the sea; west of it the coast turns north-west to Gullwick

town.why: brief 2: on the west bank, the lowest bridging point

bridge.why: old stone arches from both banks to the island with the toll house, an iron swing span over the navigation channel on the east (W7, the swing span stuck open; the way is not this PR)
bridge.from_lane_g: Lullford Bridge, centre (8976, 4312), 192 px of span, tier 3

routes._about: Inside the chunk Claude I paints these routes to lane G's line, width and tier (lib/world-routes.ts, #175; g-to-i-cells 21 Oct): 'points' are G's vertices inside the box, with 'widths' and 'tiers' per vertex; 'exits' are the cells where they leave the box. The boardwalk is Claude I's own.
